rate-calibration.title: Calibration, speed and rate
rate-calibration.caption: Synthetic lead II at 25 mm/s and 10 mm/mV. Grid and tracing share the same scale; screen millimetres vary with zoom.

rhythm-axis.title: Rhythm branch and axis
rhythm-axis.caption: Synthetic examples: sinus 75/min, a regular wide QRS rhythm at 86/min, and an irregularly irregular rhythm without discrete P waves. QRS width alone does not name a rhythm. I-positive/aVF-negative axis requires lead II.

intervals.title: PR, QRS, QTc intervals
intervals.caption: Synthetic lead II at 25 mm/s and 10 mm/mV. PR 160 ms, QRS 85 ms, and QT 380 ms to the drawn T-wave endpoint; Bazett QTc about 425 ms at 75/min.

hypertrophy.title: Voltage, Chambers and Low Voltage
hypertrophy.caption: Paper-scaled voltage schematic. Top: V1 and V5 at 5 mm/mV, converted to standard-gain Sokolow–Lyon values. Bottom: representative low-voltage lead II at 10 mm/mV; confirm the criterion across every limb lead.

omi-equivalents.title: OMI equivalents at a glance
omi-equivalents.caption: Synthetic focused examples of hyperacute T waves, de Winter morphology and Wellens type B. Lead II below is a normal rhythm reference. These are separate teaching examples, not one patient ECG.

toxic-metabolic-mimics.title: Bizarre = metabolic/toxic
toxic-metabolic-mimics.caption: Synthetic focused leads, not a patient recording or a full 12-lead. Each small box represents 40 ms / 0.1 mV at this setting. Three possible hyperkalemia appearances, not a predictable sequence or potassium-level scale.

stemi-criteria.title: Inferior STEMI pattern — II, III, aVF with aVL mirror
stemi-criteria.caption: Synthetic focused leads, not a patient recording or a full 12-lead. Each small box represents 40 ms / 0.1 mV at this setting. Convex STE II + III + aVF with mirror STD in aVL — territorial STE + mirror STD supports acute inferior occlusion.

hyperacute-t.title: Hyperacute T — normal vs hyperacute vs hyperK
hyperacute-t.caption: Synthetic focused leads, not a patient recording or a full 12-lead. Each small box represents 40 ms / 0.1 mV at this setting. Same V3 viewpoint, three T shapes: normal vs hyperacute vs hyperK tenting.

wellens.title: Wellens syndrome — Type A vs Type B
wellens.caption: Synthetic focused leads, not a patient recording or a full 12-lead. Each small box represents 40 ms / 0.1 mV at this setting. Pain-free interval after resolved angina: Type A biphasic (+/−) vs Type B deep symmetric inversion in V2–V3. Strongly associated with critical LAD disease in the appropriate clinical setting.

dewinter.title: de Winter pattern — precordial STD with tall T waves
dewinter.caption: Synthetic focused leads, not a patient recording or a full 12-lead. Each small box represents 40 ms / 0.1 mV at this setting. Upsloping J-point ST depression with tall symmetric T waves across V2–V6. aVR elevation is supportive and may be absent.

sgarbossa.title: Smith-modified Sgarbossa positive
sgarbossa.caption: Synthetic focused leads, not a patient recording or a full 12-lead. Each small box represents 40 ms / 0.1 mV at this setting. LBBB-like wide complexes: concordant anterior ST depression and concordant lateral STE are abnormal.

posterior-omi.title: Posterior OMI mirror pattern
posterior-omi.caption: Synthetic focused leads, not a patient recording or a full 12-lead. Each small box represents 40 ms / 0.1 mV at this setting. V1–V3 horizontal ST depression with dominant R and upright T raises concern for posterior occlusion. Record V7–V9 and interpret clinically.

avr-lmca.caption: Synthetic educational strip · 6 seconds · selected leads, not a full 12-lead. Grid and waveform share a calibrated scale; on-screen millimetres depend on zoom. Selected morphology, not a clinically validated patient ECG.

ischemia-map.caption: Lead and threshold teaching map; not a patient ECG. Voltage examples share the paper scale, but isolated schematic beats do not establish a diagnosis.

atrial-fibrillation.title: Atrial fibrillation
atrial-fibrillation.caption: Synthetic focused leads, not a patient recording or a full 12-lead. Each small box represents 40 ms / 0.1 mV at this setting. Irregular ventricular response without organized P waves. This example has narrow QRS complexes; it does not model pre-excitation.

normal-12lead.title: Normal sinus rhythm · full 12-lead
normal-12lead.caption: Synthetic educational 12-lead; not a patient recording. Sequential 2.5-second columns plus a 10-second lead II strip. Swipe inside the paper on phones, or Enlarge to inspect.
